rows.text: Giada rewards building an Angel count, not waiting to cast the biggest Angel in your hand. Establish cheap Angels, use Giada and cost reducers to cast multiple threats, then protect the board and finish through the air. A one-mana Angel can add more to your next three creatures than another expensive standalone threat would.

guide.title: Start small and make every Angel matter

rows.name: Giada, Font of Hope
rows.text: her counter ability modifies how other Angels enter; it is not a triggered ability. Count Angels already on the battlefield, including Giada. Angels entering simultaneously do not count each other. Giada herself receives no counters from this ability, and removing her afterward does not remove counters already placed.

Giada's white mana pays only for Angel spells. It can pay for an Angel's warp cost or a changeling creature, but not an equipment activation, protection spell, token-making ability, or non-Angel support creature. Vigilance lets her attack and still tap for mana afterward, once she is no longer summoning sick.

rows.name: Lightstall Inquisitor + Segovian Angel
rows.text: inexpensive bodies establish the count before your larger Angels enter. Inquisitor makes opponents temporarily commit a card to a more expensive spell or tapped land; it does not permanently remove those cards. Segovian's flying and vigilance make it a useful attacker and blocker once the counter engines are active.

rows.name: Youthful Valkyrie
rows.text: grows whenever another Angel enters, including a token. Deploy it early so subsequent plays grow both the newcomer through Giada and Valkyrie through its own trigger.

rows.name: Inspiring Overseer
rows.text: an Angel that replaces itself and gains a life. The life event activates the counter engines, while the additional body increases the size of later Angels.

rows.name: Lyra, Archangel of Dawn
rows.text: each life-gain event puts a counter on every Angel you control. Ten life gained at once is one trigger; life gained separately from several sources creates several triggers. This is a different card from Lyra Dawnbringer, and both can coexist.

rows.name: Archangel of Thune
rows.text: gives counters to every creature when you gain life, including your non-Angel support creatures. Its own lifelink provides an independent trigger when it deals damage.

rows.name: Bishop of Wings
rows.text: each Angel entering gains four life, and each Angel dying leaves a flying Spirit. Spirits are not Angels and receive no Giada entry counters, but they preserve blockers after a creature wipe.

rows.name: Righteous Valkyrie
rows.text: gains life equal to each other entering Angel or Cleric's toughness, including its entry counters. At 47 or more life in a normal 40-life game, its +2/+2 anthem strengthens all your creatures. The anthem switches off immediately if your life falls below that threshold.

rows.name: Angel of Vitality
rows.text: turns each life-gain event into one additional life, helping meet Resplendent Angel's five-life threshold. Four life from Bishop becomes five. Larger life gains remain a single event for Lyra and Archangel of Thune.

rows.name: Lyra Dawnbringer
rows.text: gives your other Angels +1/+1 and lifelink, while already having lifelink herself. Several lifelink creatures dealing damage together produce separate life-gain events, rapidly multiplying the team's counters through the other Lyra and Archangel of Thune.

guide.title: Turn the extra bodies into an engine

rows.name: Resplendent Angel
rows.text: checks at the beginning of EACH end step whether you gained at least five life that turn. Meeting that threshold makes a vigilant 4/4 Angel, enlarged by Giada. The token's own entry can gain more life but does not restart the same end-step trigger indefinitely.

rows.name: Luminarch Ascension
rows.text: once it has four quest counters, spare mana becomes Angels at instant speed. Its end-step condition is that you did not lose life during that opponent's turn; gaining back lost life does not repair the condition. Do not crack a life-paying fetchland during an otherwise safe opponent's turn when you need the counter.

rows.name: Exalted Sunborn
rows.text: doubles your Angel tokens, Bishop's Spirits, Treasures, Clues, and Constructs. It is also a lifelink Angel that can be warped for two mana. Angel tokens created together receive Giada counters based on the Angels already present, not on the other new tokens entering alongside them.

rows.name: Battle Angels of Tyr
rows.text: myriad supplies temporary Angel copies attacking the other opponents, and those copies receive fresh Giada counters. They do not copy counters on the original. Its combat-damage bonuses require the damaged player to have strictly more cards, lands, or life than EVERY other player for the corresponding reward; ties fail.

rows.name: Exalted Sunborn + Battle Angels of Tyr
rows.text: doubles the number of myriad tokens. That means more attacking Angels and more entry life-gain triggers, but the myriad tokens are still exiled at end of combat. They are not a permanent army.

rows.name: Roaming Throne
rows.text: choose Angel. It doubles useful triggered abilities of your other Angels, such as Righteous Valkyrie's life gain, Battle Angels' myriad, and Inspiring Overseer's entry trigger. Giada's entry-counter effect is not triggered and is NOT doubled. Abilities restricted to triggering only once per turn still respect that restriction. Throne is only a Golem spell while on the stack, so Giada's mana and Angel-specific cost reductions cannot pay for or discount it.

guide.title: Pay for threats and keep cards coming

rows.name: Starnheim Aspirant + Urza's Incubator
rows.text: each reduces an Angel spell's generic cost by two. They do not remove white pips, so a hand containing several white-intensive Angels still needs real white mana. Giada cannot supply the mana to cast either of these non-Angel cards.

rows.name: Pearl Medallion + Herald's Horn
rows.text: each removes another generic mana from qualifying spells. Medallion also helps white protection and removal; Horn names Angel and can put a qualifying top card into your hand during upkeep. Horn is not a guaranteed extra card every turn.

rows.name: Herald of War
rows.text: the ramp piece that also attacks. Each +1/+1 counter on it makes your Angel spells cost {1} less, and Giada's entry counters count, so a Herald that enters as your third Angel already discounts the next one by two. Each attack adds another counter, and Lyra, Archangel of Dawn and Archangel of Thune grow the discount whenever you gain life. It reduces only generic mana, never the white pips.

rows.name: Patchwork Banner
rows.text: name Angel. Every Angel gets +1/+1 and the Banner taps for one mana of any color, which, unlike Giada's, can pay for anything. Its bonus is not a counter, so it does not grow Herald's discount.

rows.name: Archaeomancer's Map + Land Tax
rows.text: both reward being behind on lands, which a mono-white deck usually is against green ramp. Map puts two Plains in hand at once; then whenever an opponent's land enters while that player has more lands than you, you may put a land from your hand onto the battlefield. Tax keeps the hand stocked for it. Map catches you up, which eventually switches Tax off; that is the point.

rows.name: Sol Ring + Arcane Signet + Mind Stone + Mox Amber
rows.text: cheap acceleration that, unlike Giada's mana, pays for anything: equipment, protection, removal and the non-Angel engines. Mind Stone cycles for a card once the mana stops mattering. Amber makes white once Giada or another white legendary creature is present, and produces nothing without one.

rows.name: Sword of the Animist
rows.text: equip an evasive creature and turn attacks into basic Plains. Giada's vigilance is especially useful here because she can attack, trigger the Sword, and later provide mana for an Angel.

rows.name: Land Tax + Deep Gnome Terramancer
rows.text: Tax keeps land drops in hand when an opponent is ahead; it does not put those lands onto the battlefield. Gnome ramps when opponents put lands onto the battlefield without playing them, such as through fetchlands, at most once each turn. The large Plains count supports both and the late-game Emeria plan.

rows.name: Smothering Tithe
rows.text: funds the expensive Angels and lets you leave mana for protection while developing. Opponents can pay to deny Treasures, so do not keep an otherwise nonfunctional hand based on guaranteed future Tithe mana.

rows.name: Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx + Three Tree City
rows.text: the finishing mana lands. Nykthos uses white symbols on your permanents; City names Angel and counts Angel creatures, including tokens. Both need setup and activation mana. They can produce white for spells and abilities Giada cannot pay for.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel + Folk Hero
rows.text: Sentinel supplies early cards when opponents decline its tax; Folk Hero makes the first qualifying Angel cast each turn draw while your commander has the granted ability. Folk Hero does not draw from token creation and does nothing without a suitable commander creature on the battlefield.

rows.name: Exemplar of Light
rows.text: entering with Giada's counters can draw immediately, and later life gain grows it. Its draw ability works only once per turn, so it is best with life-gain opportunities spread across the turn cycle.

rows.name: Wojek Investigator + Firemane Commando
rows.text: Investigator leaves Clues when opponents have larger hands, and Commando draws from your attacks with at least two creatures. Budget two mana to turn each Clue into a card. Commando also rewards opposing two-creature attacks aimed entirely away from you.

rows.name: The One Ring
rows.text: the primary independent refill after emptying your hand. The cast-entry protection shields you, not your creatures. Its upkeep life loss is manageable with lifelink, but do not activate blindly at a low life total or assume protection stops that life loss.

rows.name: War Room + Minas Tirith
rows.text: land slots become draw engines when you have spare mana. War Room costs one life in this mono-white deck; Minas Tirith needs you to have attacked with at least two creatures that turn. Neither requires Giada to survive.

guide.title: New Angels offer plays before turn five

rows.name: Starfield Shepherd -> Esper Sentinel
rows.text: warp Shepherd for two mana to find the early draw piece, then cast Shepherd from exile on a later turn for another search. Its other practical targets are a basic Plains, Lightstall Inquisitor, or Segovian Angel. These go to hand, not onto the battlefield.

rows.name: Astelli Reclaimer
rows.text: restores an artifact or enchantment from your graveyard based on the actual mana spent casting it. Warping for three can recover Horn or Incubator; paying five can recover Tithe or the Ring. Cost reductions shrink that maximum, and returning the Ring this way does not grant its cast-only protection.

rows.name: Flock Impostor
rows.text: a flash changeling that counts as an Angel for Giada, Horn, Incubator, and Folk Hero. Its optional bounce can save another creature, return an entry-effect creature for reuse, or pick up a warped Angel before exile. The bounced creature loses its counters and must be cast again.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares + Path to Exile
rows.text: efficient exile for a creature that threatens to stop your board or end the game. The life or land compensation is usually less important than preserving your engine. Leave real white mana available; Giada cannot cast either spell.

rows.name: Generous Gift + Stroke of Midnight
rows.text: answer noncreature problems that Angels alone cannot solve. Gift can hit any permanent; Stroke cannot target a land. The small token left behind rarely blocks a developed flying army effectively.

rows.name: Reprieve
rows.text: buy a critical turn against a spell, including one that cannot be countered. The spell returns to hand, so its owner may recast it. Use that window to finish or establish protection rather than treating it as permanent removal.

rows.name: Metropolis Reformer
rows.text: protects you from targeting and gains life when it is dealt damage. It does not give your other permanents hexproof, and sacrifice effects or damage that do not target you can still matter.

rows.name: Archangel of Tithes
rows.text: taxes opposing attacks while untapped and opposing blocks while attacking. It has no built-in vigilance, so attacking normally turns off the defensive tax until it untaps. Your mana-intensive white spells make keeping enough Plains important.

rows.name: Winds of Abandon
rows.text: overload it to exile opposing creatures while preserving your board, then attack before opponents untap with the replacement basics. It is also a two-mana single-creature answer. It does not remove artifacts or enchantments unless they are creatures.

rows.name: Ob Nixilis, the Ascended
rows.text: a one-sided creature wipe on an Angel body. When it enters it destroys every TAPPED creature your opponents control, and creatures that attacked on their own turns are still tapped during yours, so cast it after the table has swung at each other or at you. It gains 1 life per creature destroyed, and at the beginning of EACH end step, opponents' included, it makes a 4/4 flying Angel if you gained life that turn. Bishop, Seraph Sanctuary and any lifelinker turn that on nearly every turn, and Exalted Sunborn doubles the token.

rows.name: Akroma's Will
rows.text: with Giada present as you cast it, both modes give the army double strike, evasion, protection, indestructible, vigilance, and lifelink. The multiple life-gain events can generate counters between first-strike and normal combat damage, increasing the second wave. Count actual blockers and damage before committing.

rows.name: Angel of Destiny
rows.text: at your end step, with at least 55 life in a normal 40-life game, each player it attacked that turn loses. It must survive until the trigger happens, and the life condition is checked again on resolution. It need not connect, but its combat-damage life-gain ability also heals opponents and can undermine an ordinary damage plan.

rows.name: Serra's Emissary
rows.text: often choose creature to make your creatures unblockable by creatures and protect you and them from creature damage. Choose another card type when that type of targeted removal is the immediate danger. Protection from sorceries does not stop an untargeted destruction or exile spell merely because it is a sorcery.

rows.name: Avacyn, Angel of Hope
rows.text: the expensive capstone protects all your permanents from destruction and attacks as a huge vigilant flyer. It does not protect against exile, sacrifice, or toughness reduction. You do not need to wait for eight mana to win; the cheaper Angels and Will are the primary clock.

rows.name: Angelic Field Marshal
rows.text: a 5/5 flier for four while Giada is on the battlefield, and it gives every creature you control vigilance. Attack with the whole team and still keep blockers back, and still tap Giada for mana after combat. Without your commander it is a 3/3 and grants nothing.

rows.name: Angelic Field Marshal + Sephara, Sky's Blade
rows.text: Sephara's alternative cost is {W} plus tapping four untapped fliers. With vigilance from the Marshal, you can attack with everything and still pay it in your second main phase. Tapping as a cost to cast her is not a tap ability, so Angels that came in this turn can help pay.

rows.name: Sephara, Sky's Blade
rows.text: once she resolves, every other flier you control is indestructible, so destruction wipes and combat trades stop costing you the air force. It does not stop exile, sacrifice, -X/-X or bounce. She is a 7/7 lifelink flier herself, and a white legend for Mox Amber.

rows.name: Gisela, the Broken Blade
rows.text: a four-mana first-strike lifelink attacker that grows substantially through Giada. It is here for combat efficiency and reliable life gain; this list is not built around its meld ability.

rows.name: Emeria's Call
rows.text: normally an early land when you need mana, or two substantial Angel bodies late. Its indestructible clause protects NON-Angels, so it is not protection for the main Angel army. With Sunborn present, it creates four Angels instead of two.

guide.title: Keep the board and rebuild when needed

rows.name: Swiftfoot Boots
rows.text: protects Giada from targeted removal and lets her tap the turn she enters, after paying the equip cost. Hexproof still allows your own spells to target her. It does not protect against an untargeted wipe.

rows.name: Flawless Maneuver
rows.text: free while Giada is on the battlefield, and every creature you control is indestructible until end of turn. Hold it for the destruction wipe; it does not handle exile, sacrifice or toughness reduction, and Sephara already covers your other fliers against destruction while she stays.

rows.name: Guardian of Faith + Galadriel's Dismissal
rows.text: phasing preserves creatures and their counters through exile and other resets that indestructibility cannot answer. Guardian cannot phase itself with its own trigger. A kicked Dismissal can protect your whole creature board or remove an opponent's blockers temporarily for a lethal attack.

rows.name: Teferi's Protection
rows.text: protects both your life total and all your permanents through a decisive turn. Phased-out creatures have not left the battlefield, so they keep their counters and Bishop does not create Spirits.

rows.name: Serra Paragon
rows.text: once during each of your turns, play a land or cast a permanent spell with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard. A destroyed Mind Stone, Patchwork Banner, Archaeomancer's Map or cheap Angel comes back. Playing a land this way uses your land drop, and anything returned is exiled the next time it dies, so it is not unlimited recursion of the same card.

rows.name: Emeria, the Sky Ruin
rows.text: rewards the high basic Plains count with a creature returned during upkeep once you have seven other Plains. It is slow insurance, not early ramp. Prioritize a card that restores draw or protection over the biggest body when recovering from a wipe.

rows.name: Urza's Saga -> Sol Ring
rows.text: the default chapter-three target when more mana is needed. Saga sacrifices itself as its final chapter finishes, so account for losing a land. Its earlier Constructs are incidental artifact bodies, not Angels.

rows.name: Urza's Saga -> Mox Amber
rows.text: the alternative when you need unrestricted white mana and already have a white legend: Giada, Sephara, Ob Nixilis, either Lyra, Avacyn or Gisela. Saga finds only artifacts with mana cost {0} or {1}, so it cannot fetch Mind Stone, Patchwork Banner or Esper Sentinel.

Keep two or three lands with reliable white mana, Giada access through the command zone, and an early Angel, accelerator, or draw engine. A two-land hand needs a credible next land or cheap plays; a hand of Avacyn, Emissary, and several five-drops is a mulligan despite its late power. Avoid opening hands overloaded with colorless utility lands.

A good start is a one-mana Angel, Sentinel or Sol Ring on turn one, Giada on turn two, then a three- or four-mana Angel or Patchwork Banner on turn three. Giada's mana is available only once she can tap. With extra mana, deploying a cheap Angel before a larger one increases the latter's entry counters; do the arithmetic before spending Giada's restricted mana. Herald of War should attack every turn it safely can, since each attack makes the rest of your hand cheaper.

Keep one protection spell available once you have a threatening board. Spreading all resources into a fourth large Angel can be worse than keeping the first three safe. Use draw engines before the hand empties, and reserve the most expensive threats for when you can cast them without abandoning interaction.

Life thresholds care about different things: Righteous Valkyrie wants a current total of 47, Angel of Destiny wants 55, Resplendent Angel wants five life gained during that turn, and Luminarch Ascension wants no life lost that opponent's turn. Track them separately. Cast a flash Angel early enough to gain life BEFORE an end step begins if you want Resplendent to trigger there.

The deck wins through accumulated flying pressure, usually with a protection spell or Will backing the decisive attack. There is no intentional infinite combo. Its main weaknesses are repeated commander removal, exile wipes, and spell-based combo decks that can ignore combat; apply pressure and preserve the appropriate answer instead of trying to gain an arbitrary amount of life.
